headline: You learn Rust by building things yourself, questioning the machinery, and asking for feedback once you have something to test.

archetype.name: The Hands-On Questioner
archetype.description: You treat the assistant as a tutor and reviewer while keeping the implementation in your own hands. Your prompts move from ownership puzzles to CLI tools and browser games, with frequent stops to ask why something works, whether your code is idiomatic, and which edge cases you missed. A successful compile earns a celebration—and then another question.

dimensions.title: Try, review, refine
dimensions.summary: You prefer guidance that leaves you responsible for the code. You break learning into small attempts, then ask for reviews of logic, style, and edge cases before moving forward.

evidence.quote: Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator. can you check my logic?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

dimensions.title: Brief, candid, specific
dimensions.summary: You use short, informal English prompts and readily expose your current understanding. You also specify the teaching format you want, including when the assistant should wait and let you try.

evidence.quote: I thought I only had one mutable reference.
quiz me on Rust traits, 5 questions, wait for my answers
I want to add collision detection. explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it

dimensions.title: Rust through real projects
dimensions.summary: You begin with Python as a reference point for Rust, then practice serialization, argument parsing, and error handling through a CLI. Your later prompts explore browser WebAssembly and game systems, while your trait answers show an emerging vocabulary for dispatch and vtables.

evidence.quote: I'm new to Rust. Can you explain ownership like I'm a Python developer?
I'm stuck on step 3, how do I serialize a Vec of structs to JSON with serde?
Can I run Rust in the browser? I want to make a small game with WebAssembly
1: a trait is like an interface. 2: impl Trait in argument position is static dispatch. 3: dyn needs a vtable

dimensions.title: Mechanisms and trade-offs
dimensions.summary: You want explanations of the decisions underneath an API or technique. Runtime borrowing, executor choices, and game-system correctness catch your attention because you want to understand when an approach makes sense.

evidence.quote: so RefCell moves the borrow check to runtime? that feels dangerous, why is it allowed?
is tokio the only option? what are the trade-offs with smol?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

dimensions.title: Make understanding testable
dimensions.summary: You turn explanations into exercises, quizzes, and project work. Your prompts broaden from Rust fundamentals into game development, and you explicitly ask for mistakes to be explained and future learning to be structured.

evidence.quote: can you give me 3 small exercises about lifetimes?
what should I learn next to get better at game dev in Rust? give me a roadmap
what did I get wrong? explain the ones I missed

traits.name: You keep the keyboard
traits.description: You repeatedly ask for steps, explanations, and review while reserving the implementation for yourself.

evidence.quote: Don't write it for me, just give me the steps.
don't fix them, just tell me
I want to add collision detection. explain AABB first, then let me try to implement it

traits.name: Why comes after what
traits.description: You follow technical explanations and fixes with questions about the mechanism or trade-off behind them.

evidence.quote: so RefCell moves the borrow check to runtime? that feels dangerous, why is it allowed?
is tokio the only option? what are the trade-offs with smol?
oh it was the requestAnimationFrame closure being dropped. why does that happen?

traits.name: Compilation is a milestone
traits.description: You celebrate working code, then continue toward tests, idiomatic design, and overlooked cases.

evidence.quote: it compiles now!! next step: how do I write tests for the CLI?
can you review it and point out non-idiomatic parts?
here is my AABB function, any edge cases I missed?

traits.name: You invite the red pen
traits.description: You make your understanding visible through answers and implementations, then actively ask where it falls short.

evidence.quote: here's my answer to exercise 1, is it idiomatic?
I implemented a fixed timestep with an accumulator. can you check my logic?
what did I get wrong? explain the ones I missed
